transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Ben Reyes (BlueSlate CTO), Nora Li (Head of Infra), Samir Patel (SRE), Janel Gomez (PM)

Summary:
Quick postmortem follow-up for last week's elevated error-rate window attributed to cache staleness and a replay storm during a partial rollout. Goal: align on root causes, runbook updates, test plan for KV-cache replay, and next actions to avoid recurrence.

Topics:
- Observed symptom timeline and suspected cache invalidation gap
- Replay amplification from client-side retries and circuit-breaker gaps
- Where Redwood falling back to alternate model variants and implications
- Runbook changes: protective throttles, rollout gating, and emergency rollback steps
- Security/access requests for logs and telemetry

Action items (captured above): run cache replay test, share configs, update runbook, give log access.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Martinez: hey everybody, thanks for joining. we wanted to keep this tight, 60, 75 max. um, quick recap first 	6 last thursday around 03:12 UTC you had a p95 latency climb and a flurry of 5xxs, is that the window we all have in mind?
[00:18] Ben Reyes: yeah that's right, it started as a small blip during the canary rollout then, yeah, it, it escalated once the client retries kicked in. we saw some nodes that had stale prefix caches and then the kv, kv cash 	6 sorry 	6 the KV cache didn't evict as expected.
[00:34] Priya Shah: (laughs) K-V cash, that's the one I see in the logs sometimes too. can you confirm which model variant you were routing to? was it rwd-14g-quant or the fallback 14g-qat?
[00:45] Nora Li: we were on rwd-14g-quant for the canary, and the fallback only triggered after the first couple of failures. our edge retry policy is aggressive 	6 it's 3 immediate retries with exponential backoff, but the backoff baseline is small so it amplifies.
[01:05] Samir Patel: the amplification is key. the client side hits retry then the request lands, runtime tries to fetch the kv-prefix from cache and misses, then backend does a synchronous regen which is expensive, that regen plus subsequent requests led to CPU spikes and some token-level timeouts.
[01:23] Alex Martinez: okay, interesting. from our side the runtime saw a lot of concurrent prefix misses for identical keys, and our autoscaler warmed nodes but the regen path is heavier. we had a fallback to the 14g-qat variant for some tenants but that introduced higher latency for others.
[01:42] Janel Gomez: just to add, product saw some downstream user errors in the UI 	6 timeouts and retry loops; PM asked for clearer downgrade messaging but that's downstream. today we need the technical steps.
[01:55] Priya Shah: can I ask Samir to, uh, quickly outline the cache eviction TTLs and any manual tuning done for the canary? I noticed in your ticket there were a few manual adjustments.
[02:10] Samir Patel: sure 	6 TTLs were mostly default (60s for prefix entries), but we did bump to 300s on two nodes to cut regen load after we saw thrashing. hindsight: that probably widened the staleness window.
[02:25] Ben Reyes: we did that to damp load, yes, but that allowed stale prefixes to remain longer, so when we later pushed the corrected weights the cache contained old prefixes and clients kept hitting them.
[02:36] Alex Martinez: that's the classic latency-vs-consistency trade-off. Ideally the runtime should detect a canary-related model schema change and proactively invalidate prefixes. we have a proposal in the optimization doc but it's not live for that release.
[02:51] Priya Shah: right 	6 we have an invalidation hook that can be triggered by model-id + version. the issue here seemed to be that the canary rollout mutated internal weight matrices but didn't change the model version metadata, so the invalidation didn't run.
[03:10] Nora Li: correct, because our deploy pipeline only bumps version for explicit model changes. this time the change was parameter-only.
[03:20] Alex Martinez: that's an important lesson. we should add a gating check in your CI that ensures any parameter diff which affects KV keys causes a metadata version bump or triggers a cache invalidation call.
[03:35] Ben Reyes: agreed. who owns that? BlueSlate or Redwood?
[03:40] Alex Martinez: recommendation 	6 double responsibility. BlueSlate's CD to signal the change, Redwood to provide an API endpoint for invalidation and also a safemode that automatically invalidates when model weights exceed a delta threshold.
[03:55] Priya Shah: we can prototype the safemode, but it needs telemetry thresholds. for the immediate fix I'm recommending a replay test: reproduce the regen path offline against staging so we can validate throttle and queueing behavior without affecting prod.
[04:12] Samir Patel: can you run that against our production trace? I'll export a 1-hour window with request ids and attach the requestId -> cacheKey mapping. it's noisy but should be fine.
[04:22] Priya Shah: perfect, please share that mapping. I'll run the replay with three configs: default TTL, increased TTL (300s), and invalidation on deploy, to show the delta.
[04:34] Alex Martinez: that'll help quantify how many regen ops and concurrent token cost we're talking about. also we'll capture p50/p95/p99 for latency and CPU curves.
[04:45] Janel Gomez: can we also include an estimate of egress cost? product wants a rough $ delta to present to execs.
[04:55] Alex Martinez: yes we can add a cost delta. it's coarse but useful.
[05:02] Ben Reyes: there was also an observation about our client retry config 	6 we should gate immediate retries when an endpoint returns specific transient codes, maybe use 429 semantics and let the runtime respond with a 429 rather than 5xx.
[05:18] Priya Shah: good call. we can add a soft-throttle response that instructs clients to back off for X ms. currently the runtime doesn't expose a backoff header. we can add that as a short-term mitigation.
[05:30] Nora Li: about the runbook 	6 what I need is a crisp rollback criteria and an emergency throttle value to set from our side. our oncall will want a single page checklist.
[05:42] Alex Martinez: absolutely. we'll provide a one-page runbook snippet: 1) set throttle to 40% token throughput, 2) flip model-route to fallback variant, 3) invalidate caches, 4) escalate to Redwood SE. we'll send that as 'runbook-snippet-v1'.
[05:57] Samir Patel: please include commands for cache invalidation. we prefer CLI examples and curl calls.
[06:04] Priya Shah: copy, i'll include curl and SDK snippets (node/python) and a small note about node drain.
[06:18] Alex Martinez: (laughs) the transcript will keep that.
[06:22] [pause/background talking as participants look up dashboards]
[06:50] Ben Reyes: on telemetry, what extra traces do you need? we currently sample token traces at 0.5% and error traces at 100%.
[07:02] Priya Shah: token traces are heavy. for the replay test we need full request logs for the window you're sharing, specifically cacheKey, requestId, modelVariantId, and backend node. 0.5% won't cut it for reproducing regen contention.
[07:19] Nora Li: we'll up the sampling for that window and give you the full dump to the shared bucket. note: security, we need Redwood to use our read-only role and confirm audit logs won't be altered.
[07:32] Alex Martinez: we'll use a temporary read-only IAM role and confirm all accesses appear in your audit logs. we'll also provide a signed NDA-style note if that helps internal compliance.
[07:44] Samir Patel: also want to call out 	6 a couple of times the runtime's fallback decision picked higher latency variant for subsets; curious how fallback scoring worked.
[07:54] Priya Shah: our fallback scoring uses a weighted function of failure rate + queue depth + latency. if queue depth on the warm path exceeds threshold and failure rate spikes, it flips. sometimes the scoring can be noisy in partial rollouts; we can add a hysteresis buffer.
[08:10] Alex Martinez: hysteresis would reduce flip-flop during canaries. good engineering item.
[08:18] [10-minute jump in transcript captured as participants review artifacts]
[18:20] Priya Shah: ok i ran a quick dry-run in staging earlier this morning 	6 initial results show that invalidation-on-deploy removes ~78% of regen ops for the trace we used. increased TTL reduces regen spikes but increases staleness windows, so it's a trade.
[18:40] Ben Reyes: so for immediate mitigation you recommend invalidation-on-deploy rather than increasing TTL.
[18:46] Priya Shah: yes, short-term invalidation plus softer client retries. medium-term add canary metadata gating and safemode. long-term we want automatic detection by token-delta thresholds.
[18:58] Nora Li: acceptable. for the runbook handoff we need: clear rollout gating steps, immediate mitigation (curl examples), who to call at Redwood (oncall + SE contact), and an escalation timeline.
[19:14] Alex Martinez: we'll include Redwood oncall alias and a 24/7 emergency path for Dedicated and Private accounts. for Hosted we have a support SL of 4 hours but we can agree on a faster path for you in the contract addendum.
[19:29] Janel Gomez: we'll review contract addendum with legal, likely OK.
[19:35] Priya Shah: i'm going to note one more technical gotcha: if clients do sticky routing to an edge that had the bumped TTL, they may keep seeing stale prefixes even after invalidation calls routed to other nodes. so the runbook should include a global rolling invalidation and a node drain step.
[19:52] Samir Patel: noted. we'll do a drain sequence and then re-enable traffic.
[20:00] [brief cross talk about test schedule]
[20:20] Alex Martinez: last bit 	6 competitors. Ben, you had asked about how VendorX handles this; they do more conservative TTL by default but that tends to cost more. Anthropic's managed offering exposes more tuning knobs but they also charge for token regen. just context.
[20:36] Ben Reyes: yep, cost vs reliability. we'll factor that in.
[20:41] Alex Martinez: ok closing recap 	6 Priya will run replay on the mapping Samir provides and share results + graphs; Alex will send runbook-snippet-v1 with CLI commands; BlueSlate will grant temp read-only log access; follow-up meeting week of 2026-09-13 to review.
[20:55] Nora Li: sounds good. thank you all.
[21:00] Meeting ends.

Notes about transcript quality: intermittent mis-transcriptions on acronyms (KV vs K-V cash) and some overlapping talk labeled as laughter or pauses. timestamps are approximate; full logs and attachments will be added to CRM.
